title: Communication and the communication management approach
blurb: Explain why communication is vital in an agile project and what the communication management approach covers.
question: A health project sends the same monthly update to every group and relies on reports to judge progress, but resistance keeps surprising the team. What does PRINCE2 Agile say good communication looks like?

teach.body: Good communication avoids misconceptions and unnecessary barriers to change. In an agile project, work moves in short iterations, priorities shift and many groups are affected, so information has to flow quickly and both ways. Agile thinking prefers rich communication: words plus visuals, conversation and body language, which leaves little room for misunderstanding. In plain English: if people are not hearing and being heard, the change stalls.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 7 manual 3.4; PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.4, 2.7.3

teach.body: The communication management approach defines and describes the means and frequency of communication with, and receiving feedback from, across the project ecosystem, supporting alignment and shaping of the project. It sets up a controlled and bidirectional flow of information. It is as much about listening as broadcasting: understanding people's perceptions and concerns and addressing them before they become bigger risks, and tailoring messages to the interests of different groups. It is agreed in initiating a project.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.4, Table 4.1; Table 13.6

teach.body: Generic messaging is rarely effective, because people get information from many channels. Working with key influencers from the user, supplier and business stakeholder groups brings in different perspectives, strengthens feedback loops and allows tailored messages for each group. Most communication happens outside formal channels anyway, so accept it: provide information in formats people can share, and offer several ways to give feedback.

teach.body: Larchfield Community Health is moving district nurses to a mobile records app. Project manager Femi Adeyemi stops the single monthly newsletter. In the communication management approach he sets out short demo videos nurses can share, a weekly drop-in call and an anonymous feedback form. He works with a respected nurse lead, the supplier's trainer and a finance manager as key influencers to tailor messages for each group. For the remote supplier team he agrees how information flows and keeps some informal call time.

teach.text: The communication management approach is not where agile behaviours are documented: that is the quality management approach. Nor is it a one-way broadcast plan. Its job is the means and frequency of communication and feedback, two ways, across the whole ecosystem.

items: Communication avoids misconceptions and unnecessary barriers to change.
Communication management approach: means and frequency of communication and feedback (Table 4.1).
Controlled, bidirectional flow; as much listening as broadcasting.
Generic messages rarely work; tailor through key influencers in each group.
Accept informal channels; give shareable formats and many feedback routes.
Periodic reports alone can be biased; remote teams need deliberate structure.

summary: You can now explain why communication is vital in agile projects and what the communication management approach defines. You can also recognize good practice: two-way flow, tailored messages through key influencers, informal channels accepted, and deliberate structure for remote teams.

A.q: What is the purpose of the communication management approach?
options: To document the agile behaviours the teams will follow
To define the target state and how the business moves to it from now
To define the means and frequency of communication and feedback
To record each stakeholder concern as a formal issue
A.why: Its purpose is to define and describe the means and frequency of communication with, and receiving feedback from, across the project ecosystem (Table 4.1).

whyNot.0: Agile behaviours are documented in the quality management approach.
whyNot.1: The target state and transition are described in the change management approach.
whyNot.3: Concerns are listened to and addressed; not every concern is a formal issue.

A.q: Which BEST describes the flow of information the communication management approach establishes?
options: Top-down and on a periodic cycle
Controlled and bidirectional
Informal and largely unrecorded
One-way, by broadcast to everyone
A.why: It facilitates engagement through a controlled and bidirectional flow of information (book 4.4).

whyNot.0: Top-down periodic updates miss the feedback the approach exists to gather.
whyNot.2: The flow is controlled and planned, even though informal channels are accepted.
whyNot.3: The approach is as much about listening as broadcasting.

A.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. A communication management approach is equally about [?] as it is about broadcasting.
options: reporting
escalating
recording
listening
A.why: Book 4.4: the approach is equally about listening as broadcasting, seeking to understand people's perceptions and concerns.

whyNot.0: Reporting is one way of broadcasting; the contrast is with listening.
whyNot.1: Escalation belongs to the progress and issues practices.
whyNot.2: Recording is not the counterpart the book draws.

B.q: Why does PRINCE2 Agile warn against relying on periodic reporting alone to judge a change initiative?
options: Reporting is replaced by daily stand-ups in agile
Reports can be biased towards what seems acceptable
Reports are owned by project assurance, not the PM
Reporting frequency is fixed by the commercial approach
B.why: Book 4.4: reporting can be biased, as people may adjust information to what is acceptable, expected or desirable.

whyNot.0: Stand-ups coordinate the team; reporting still happens through dashboards.
whyNot.2: Ownership of reports is not the reason given; bias is.
whyNot.3: The commercial management approach covers contracts, not reporting frequency.

B.q:
Which two statements about communication in a change initiative are correct?
1. Most communication within organizations happens outside formal channels.
2. Generic messaging is the most effective way to reach every group.
3. Listening helps surface concerns before they become bigger risks.
4. Informal networks should be shut down to protect message control.
options: 1 and 2
2 and 4
3 and 4
1 and 3
B.why: Most communication occurs outside formal channels, and listening addresses concerns before they become more significant risks (book 4.4).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: generic messaging is rarely effective.
whyNot.1: Both are wrong: generic messages rarely work, and informal channels should be accepted.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is wrong: informal channels are accepted and fed with shareable information.

B.q: A remote team keeps missing information. What does PRINCE2 Agile suggest focusing on?
options: Clarity on how information flows, in suitable formats
Moving all communication into formal written reports
Cutting unstructured time so that the calls stay short
Sending one standard message to all stakeholders
B.why: Book 4.4: remote teams need a more deliberate, structured approach, seeking clarity on how information flows and providing it in appropriate formats.

whyNot.1: Formal reports alone can be biased and slow; they do not fix the flow.
whyNot.2: Remote teams should agree both structured and unstructured time together.

C.q: Which management approach documents agile behaviours, and which defines the means and frequency of communication?
options: Quality approach for behaviours; communication approach for communication
Communication approach for behaviours; the change approach for communication
Change approach for behaviours; communication approach for communication
Quality approach for behaviours; change approach for communication
C.why: Agile behaviours are documented in the quality management approach; the communication management approach defines the means and frequency of communication and feedback (Table 4.1).

whyNot.1: The communication approach does not describe agile behaviours, and the change approach covers the transition.
whyNot.2: The change approach covers moving to the target state, not agile behaviours.
whyNot.3: The quality approach is right for behaviours, but communication belongs to the communication approach.

C.q: Messages about a new app are not landing with users, the supplier's staff or business managers. What is MOST likely to help?
options: Send one longer message so everyone gets the same facts
Increase the frequency of the monthly project newsletter
Work with key influencers in each group to tailor messages
Ask project assurance to approve each message before release
C.why: Book 4.4: working with key influencers from user, supplier and business groups accommodates different perspectives and enables tailored messaging.

whyNot.0: Generic messaging is rarely effective, however long it is.
whyNot.1: More of the same generic message does not tailor it to each group.
whyNot.3: Project assurance monitors governance; approval does not make messages fit each group.

C.q: A project manager tries to stop informal chats about the project to keep 'one version of the truth'. Which assessment is BEST?
options: Sound: formal channels are required on agile projects like this
Sound: informal chat creates issues for the register
Weak: switch to a single monthly report instead
Weak: accept informal channels and give shareable formats
C.why: Most communication occurs outside formal channels, so it is best to accept this, provide information in formats people can share and offer multiple feedback routes (book 4.4).

whyNot.0: No such requirement exists; informal communication is accepted.
whyNot.1: Informal discussion is not, in itself, an issue to register.
whyNot.2: Right verdict, wrong fix: periodic reporting alone is insufficient.

reteach.title: The school newsletter nobody reads
reteach.question: Why do parents still miss the sports day change when the school put it in the newsletter?

blocks.h: People hear things in many ways
blocks.body: Parents learn more from the class chat group and the playground than from the newsletter. A wise head teacher sends a short message parents can forward, asks class reps (the key influencers) to pass it on in their own words, and gives an easy way to ask questions. Projects work the same way: tailor, use the channels people really use, and listen.

blocks.text: Sending more of the same message is not better communication. Listening and tailoring are.

explain.body: The communication management approach defines how and how often to communicate with, and receive feedback from, across the project ecosystem, through a controlled two-way flow.

test.q: The communication management approach defines the means and frequency of communication and:
options: the target organizational state to reach
the tolerances agreed for each stage
the agile behaviours expected of teams
receiving feedback from the ecosystem
test.why: It covers the means and frequency of communication with, and receiving feedback from, across the project ecosystem (Table 4.1).

whyNot.0: The target state belongs to the change management approach.
whyNot.1: Stage tolerances are set by the project board.
whyNot.2: Agile behaviours are documented in the quality management approach.

explain.body: Generic messaging is rarely effective. Key influencers from the user, supplier and business groups help accommodate different perspectives and tailor messages for each group.

test.q: Generic messaging to all stakeholder groups is:
options: rarely effective, so messages are tailored
the preferred method in agile projects
required by the change management approach
the role of the project executive
test.why: Book 4.4: generic messaging is rarely effective; tailored messaging through key influencers works better.

whyNot.2: The change management approach covers the transition, not message wording.
whyNot.3: Communication is shared work, not a duty set on the executive.

explain.body: Most communication happens outside formal channels. Accept it, provide information in formats people can share, and offer several feedback routes.

test.q: Since most communication happens outside formal channels, a project should:
options: ban informal discussion of the project
route all questions through the PM
provide shareable formats and feedback routes
move all updates into the project highlight report
test.why: Book 4.4: accept informal communication, provide information in multiple shareable formats and offer multiple pathways for feedback.

whyNot.0: Banning informal talk ignores how people really communicate.
whyNot.1: A single route through the PM bottlenecks feedback.
whyNot.3: One report cannot reach people through the channels they use.

explain.body: Remote teams need a more deliberate, structured approach: clear information flow, suitable formats, key relationships identified, and agreed structured and unstructured time together. Hybrid teams combine both.

test.q: For a remote team, PRINCE2 Agile suggests agreeing:
options: structured time without informal chat, to save effort
both structured and unstructured time
weekly written reports in place of calls
a ban on informal online conversation
test.why: Book 4.4: remote teams identify key relationships and agree how to build both structured and unstructured time together.

whyNot.0: Unstructured time also matters for remote teams.
whyNot.2: Written reports alone are insufficient and can be biased.
whyNot.3: Informal conversation helps relationships; it is not banned.
